html:
The Khatyn massacre was the killing of 149 people of the village of Khatyn, near Minsk, on 22 March 1943 by a German SS unit and auxiliary police, as a reprisal for a partisan attack.

The villagers, about half of them children, were herded into a barn that was set on fire; those who escaped the flames were shot. Khatyn was one of more than 600 Belarusian villages burned with all or most of their people during the German occupation. Belarus lost around a quarter of its population in World War II, counting the Jews killed in the Holocaust. The Khatyn memorial, opened in 1969, has a chimney and a bell for each house. Partisan warfare and these losses are central to the memory of Belarus.
